newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes barely changed in holiday market.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes barely changed in holiday market.

text.p: Gold and silver prices were barely changed from Friday levels on Monday morning but the platinum and palladium markets were both sharply firmer.
Dealers said continuing tightness in platinum group metal coupled with a limit-up move for the fourth consecutive day on Japan's Tocom futures market ensured higher prices in Europe.
"There simply isn't enough metal, especially palladium, around," one dealer said.
Platinum fixed at $442.00 per ounce on Monday up nine dollars from Friday and palladium was at $233.00, up six dollars.
At the gold fixing bullion was set at $324.05 just five cents down from Friday when bullion closed at $324.00/$324.50.
Dealers said they were looking for gold to drift lower on Monday, possibly testing $321.00 if the interim support at $324.00 broke down.

They noted selling from Australian and Japanese interests in Hong Kong had put a little pressure on the price. "But there is very little involvement this morning. The summer season is truly upon us," one dealer said.
Trading volumes on the foreign exchanges were light too but the dollar spiralled to over 1.87 marks for the first time since October 1989 and rose against the other European currencies.
The strong dollar was all but choking off investor demand in Europe due to its strength pushing bullion to uncompetitive levels in local currencies.
Silver was two cents firmer from Friday at $4.46/$4.48 but extremely quiet and showing no sign of positioning to fill the $4.50-$4.55 chart gap showing up on the Comex futures market.
Even so, the outlook for silver remained relatively bullish compared to gold with a target of the resistance at $4.80-$4.90 tentatively set.

Most of platinum's strength was coming from the much tighter palladium market, some dealers said, although it still commanded a borrowing rate of around 35 percent for a month, about half the rate demanded for borrowing palladium.
"There is enough platinum in Europe to satisfy demand," one dealer said.
Prices of the platinum group metals have soared this year due administrative problems preventing the major exporter Russia from delivering between December and July.
Deliveries to Japan and Europe have been sporadic since they began last month and have not yet lifted the market tightness.
